title: Vaccination and Conditional Pathogen Invasion in a Malaria Meningococcal Model with Disease Specific Immunity
content: Vaccination against one pathogen can alter invasion by another through changes in resident infection and immune histories. We analyse an autonomous malaria-meningococcal model with fifteen human compartments preserving pathogen-specific vaccination and immunity, together with three mosquito compartments. We establish non-negativity and boundedness, derive disease-free thresholds, obtain an exact vaccination-rate criterion, and construct six- and seven-dimensional conditional invasion operators. A transmission-parameter symmetry establishes structural non-identifiability. The disease-free threshold is the maximum of the two pathogen components. Increasing vaccination reduces meningococcal invasion exactly when the vaccinated breakthrough pathway has a smaller transmission-weighted duration than the unvaccinated pathway. Conditional invasion can exceed one even when the corresponding disease-free component is below one. Mosquito biting frequency and the two per-bite transmission probabilities cannot be identified separately because the equations depend only on two products. Numerical examples compare conditional matrices with full-system Jacobian blocks and small-introduction trajectories. The results distinguish disease-free control from invasion into a resident-pathogen population and clarify the interpretation of transmission parameters. Simulations illustrate theoretical mechanisms; they do not estimate vaccine effectiveness or establish global elimination.
